title: Technology & Internet
subtitle: Talk about your phone, what you do online, and what to say when nothing works

lessons.title: Mon téléphone
lessons.description: Name your devices and apps, and use the everyday verbs of switching on, downloading and installing.

blocks.heading: Les appareils : your devices
blocks.body: Un appareil is any device or gadget. In everyday French people say un portable for a mobile phone, and un ordinateur portable for a laptop — context makes it clear which one you mean. Most device words are masculine (le téléphone, le clavier, le chargeur), but watch out for la tablette, la souris and la batterie, which are feminine.

examples.french: J'ai un nouveau portable depuis lundi.
examples.english: I've had a new mobile since Monday.

examples.french: Mon ordinateur portable est dans mon sac.
examples.english: My laptop is in my bag.
examples.note: un portable alone = phone; un ordinateur portable = laptop

blocks.tip: In text messages the French shorten un téléphone portable to un tél or simply mon tel — but say le portable when you speak.

blocks.heading: Allumer, éteindre, télécharger, installer
blocks.body: Four verbs cover most of what you do with a device. Allumer means to switch on and éteindre to switch off; éteindre is irregular (j'éteins, nous éteignons, past participle éteint). Télécharger means both to download and to upload, and installer means to install an app. All three of allumer, télécharger and installer are regular -er verbs.

examples.french: J'allume mon ordinateur tous les matins à huit heures.
examples.english: I switch my computer on every morning at eight.

examples.french: Éteins la télé, s'il te plaît.
examples.english: Turn the TV off, please.

examples.french: J'ai téléchargé une application de météo.

examples.french: Elle installe le jeu sur sa tablette.

examples.english: We switch our phones off during meals.

examples.english: The phone switched itself off.

blocks.tip: Say allumer / éteindre for anything electric — a lamp, an oven, a computer. For a car engine the French prefer démarrer.

blocks.heading: Les applications et ce qu'on en fait
blocks.body: Une application is an app, shortened to une appli in conversation. To say what an app is for, use pour + infinitive: une appli pour apprendre les langues. To say you use something, the verb is utiliser, and to say you press a button, appuyer sur.

examples.english: I use an app to learn Spanish.

blocks.heading: The verb éteindre (and its family)
blocks.body: Éteindre belongs to a small group of -eindre verbs (éteindre, peindre, atteindre). The singular forms lose the d: j'éteins, tu éteins, il éteint. The plural adds gn: nous éteignons, vous éteignez, ils éteignent. The past participle is éteint, used with avoir: j'ai éteint.

examples.french: J'éteins mon ordinateur à six heures.
examples.english: I switch my computer off at six.

examples.french: Tu éteins la lumière, s'il te plaît ?
examples.english: Will you switch the light off, please?

examples.english: We switch the screens off after dinner.

examples.english: They switch their phones off at the cinema.

examples.french: Hier soir, j'ai éteint la télé très tard.
examples.english: Last night I switched the TV off very late.

blocks.tip: Allumer is completely regular, so you only have one irregular verb to learn in this pair.

blocks.heading: Giving instructions: the imperative
blocks.body: To tell someone what to do, drop the subject pronoun. For tu with an -er verb, also drop the final -s: tu allumes → Allume ! For vous, keep the normal form: Allumez ! To say don't, wrap the verb in ne … pas: N'éteins pas l'ordinateur.

examples.french: Allume le wifi, s'il te plaît.
examples.english: Turn the wifi on, please.
examples.note: tu form of an -er verb loses the -s

examples.note: éteindre is not an -er verb, so it keeps the -s

blocks.tip: Adding s'il te plaît or s'il vous plaît turns any imperative into a polite request.

passages.title: Le nouveau téléphone de Lucas
passages.french:
Lucas a acheté un nouveau portable samedi dernier.
Il l'a allumé tout de suite dans le magasin.
Le vendeur lui a expliqué comment installer les applications.
À la maison, Lucas a téléchargé une appli de musique et deux jeux.
Il a aussi mis une photo de son chien comme fond d'écran.
Le soir, la batterie était déjà presque vide.
« C'est normal le premier jour », a dit sa sœur.
Elle lui a conseillé d'éteindre le wifi la nuit.
Depuis, Lucas charge son téléphone pendant qu'il dort.
Maintenant la batterie tient toute la journée.
passages.english:
Lucas bought a new mobile last Saturday.
He switched it on straight away in the shop.
The salesman explained to him how to install apps.
At home, Lucas downloaded a music app and two games.
He also put a photo of his dog as his wallpaper.
In the evening the battery was already almost empty.
"That's normal on the first day," his sister said.
She advised him to switch the wifi off at night.
Since then, Lucas charges his phone while he sleeps.
Now the battery lasts all day.

lessons.title: En ligne
lessons.description: Talk about the internet and social media, and replace nouns with the pronouns le, la and les.

blocks.heading: Se connecter à Internet
blocks.body: Internet takes no article in French: je cherche sur Internet. But the connection itself is la connexion and the network is le wifi or le réseau. To log in is se connecter, to log out se déconnecter, and to sign up s'inscrire — all reflexive verbs, so they need me, te, se in front.

examples.french: Je me connecte à Internet avec mon portable.
examples.english: I connect to the internet with my phone.

examples.english: She signed up on the site yesterday.
examples.note: reflexive verbs take être in the passé composé

examples.english: Don't forget to log out.

examples.french: J'achète presque tout en ligne.

blocks.tip: The French say le mail or un mail far more often than un courriel, which sounds official or Canadian.

blocks.heading: Les réseaux sociaux
blocks.body: Un réseau social is a social network; the plural is les réseaux sociaux, because words in -eau take -x and social becomes sociaux. On a network you have un compte and un profil, you publish une publication, you leave un commentaire, and you have des abonnés, followers.

blocks.tip: Liker and poster are borrowed from English and conjugate like normal -er verbs: j'ai liké, elle a posté.

blocks.heading: Ce qu'on fait sur Internet
blocks.body: The most useful verbs online are chercher (to look for), trouver (to find), cliquer sur (to click on), partager (to share), publier (to post), suivre (to follow) and supprimer (to delete). Note that you click sur something, and that suivre is irregular: je suis, tu suis, il suit, nous suivons.

blocks.heading: Direct object pronouns: le, la, les
blocks.body: To avoid repeating a noun, replace it with a pronoun: le for a masculine noun, la for a feminine one, les for any plural. Unlike English, the pronoun goes BEFORE the verb, not after it. Before a vowel or a silent h, le and la become l'.

examples.french: Tu connais ce site ? — Oui, je le connais.
examples.english: Do you know this site? — Yes, I know it.

examples.french: Tu as ma photo ? — Oui, je la garde.
examples.english: Do you have my photo? — Yes, I'm keeping it.

examples.french: Tes mots de passe ? Je les note dans un carnet.
examples.english: Your passwords? I write them down in a notebook.

examples.french: Cette application, je l'utilise tous les jours.
examples.english: That app, I use it every day.

examples.french: Je ne le partage avec personne.
examples.english: I don't share it with anyone.
examples.note: in the negative, ne comes before the pronoun

blocks.tip: Word order in French is subject + pronoun + verb: je le regarde. Saying je regarde le is always wrong.

blocks.heading: Pronouns with two verbs and in the past
blocks.body: When there are two verbs, the pronoun sits just before the infinitive: je vais le télécharger. In the passé composé it goes before the auxiliary: je l'ai téléchargé. And there the past participle agrees with the pronoun: je les ai supprimées if the noun is feminine plural.

examples.french: Je vais le télécharger ce soir.
examples.english: I'm going to download it tonight.
examples.note: pronoun in front of the infinitive

examples.french: Ces messages ? Je les ai supprimés hier.

examples.note: ne … pas wraps around the auxiliary

blocks.tip: In the imperative the pronoun jumps behind the verb with a hyphen: Regarde-le ! Partage-la !

passages.title: Une semaine sans réseaux sociaux
passages.french:
Camille passe deux heures par jour sur les réseaux sociaux.
Elle regarde des vidéos, elle like des photos et elle laisse des commentaires.
Lundi dernier, elle a décidé d'arrêter pendant une semaine.
Elle a supprimé les applis de son téléphone, mais elle a gardé son compte.
Les deux premiers jours ont été difficiles.
« Je prenais mon portable sans réfléchir », explique-t-elle.
Ensuite, elle a lu deux livres et elle a appelé ses amies.
Le dimanche soir, elle a réinstallé une seule application.
Maintenant elle la consulte le soir, vingt minutes maximum.
Elle dit qu'elle dort beaucoup mieux depuis.
passages.english:
Camille spends two hours a day on social media.
She watches videos, she likes photos and she leaves comments.
Last Monday she decided to stop for a week.
She deleted the apps from her phone, but she kept her account.
The first two days were hard.
"I used to pick up my phone without thinking," she explains.
After that, she read two books and she called her friends.
On Sunday evening she reinstalled one single app.
Now she checks it in the evening, twenty minutes maximum.
She says she has been sleeping much better since then.

lessons.title: Un problème technique
lessons.description: Explain what is broken, describe what does not work, and ask someone for help.

blocks.heading: Ça ne marche pas : saying it doesn't work
blocks.body: The everyday way to say something doesn't work is ça ne marche pas, often shortened in speech to ça marche pas. A slightly more technical alternative is ça ne fonctionne pas. If a machine breaks down completely, it is en panne, and the moment of breaking down is tomber en panne.

examples.french: Mon ordinateur ne marche plus.
examples.english: My computer doesn't work any more.

examples.french: L'imprimante ne fonctionne pas depuis ce matin.
examples.english: The printer hasn't been working since this morning.

examples.french: Ma voiture est en panne.
examples.english: My car has broken down.

examples.french: Le téléphone est tombé en panne hier.
examples.english: The phone broke down yesterday.

examples.french: L'écran est cassé, mais le reste marche.
examples.english: The screen is broken, but the rest works.

examples.french: Rien ne marche aujourd'hui !
examples.english: Nothing is working today!

blocks.tip: Marcher literally means to walk — the French use the same verb for machines, which is a useful image: the machine is walking along fine.

blocks.heading: Décrire le problème
blocks.body: To describe the problem, start with the thing that fails and add a simple verb: l'application se ferme toute seule, la page ne s'ouvre pas, le son ne marche pas. To say since when, use depuis + a time: depuis hier, depuis deux jours. To say what happened, use the passé composé.

examples.french: L'application se ferme toute seule.
examples.english: The app closes on its own.

examples.french: L'ordinateur est très lent depuis la mise à jour.
examples.english: The computer has been very slow since the update.

examples.french: J'ai perdu tous mes documents.
examples.english: I lost all my documents.

examples.french: Il n'y a plus de son.
examples.english: There's no sound any more.

examples.french: Le clavier est bloqué.
examples.english: The keyboard is stuck.

examples.french: Ça a planté au milieu du film.
examples.english: It crashed in the middle of the film.
examples.note: planter = to crash, very common in speech

blocks.tip: Depuis + present is the normal French pattern where English uses a perfect: il est lent depuis hier = it has been slow since yesterday.

blocks.heading: Demander de l'aide
blocks.body: To ask for help politely, use pourriez-vous or est-ce que vous pouvez + infinitive. Two very useful nouns are l'aide (help) and le service client (customer service). If you want someone to have a look, say jeter un œil, and to repair is réparer.

examples.french: Est-ce que vous pouvez m'aider, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.english: Can you help me, please?

examples.french: Pourriez-vous jeter un œil à mon téléphone ?
examples.english: Could you take a look at my phone?

examples.french: J'ai besoin d'aide avec mon ordinateur.
examples.english: I need help with my computer.

examples.french: Combien coûte la réparation ?
examples.english: How much does the repair cost?

examples.french: J'ai appelé le service client trois fois.
examples.english: I called customer service three times.

examples.french: Vous pouvez le réparer aujourd'hui ?
examples.english: Can you repair it today?

blocks.tip: Aider takes a direct object: aidez-moi, not aidez à moi. But avoir besoin needs de: j'ai besoin d'aide.

blocks.heading: Negation beyond ne … pas
blocks.body: French negation is a sandwich: ne goes before the verb and a second word after it. Ne … pas = not, ne … plus = not any more, ne … jamais = never, ne … rien = nothing. In the passé composé the sandwich wraps the auxiliary: je n'ai rien compris.

examples.french: Le son ne marche pas.
examples.english: The sound doesn't work.

examples.french: Mon ordinateur ne démarre plus.
examples.english: My computer doesn't start any more.

examples.french: Ce logiciel ne plante jamais.
examples.english: This software never crashes.

examples.french: Je n'ai rien changé, promis !
examples.english: I didn't change anything, I promise!

examples.french: Il n'y a plus de batterie.
examples.english: There's no battery left.

blocks.tip: In relaxed speech the ne almost disappears: ça marche pas, j'ai rien fait. Keep the ne when you write.

blocks.heading: Asking politely for help
blocks.body: Three levels of politeness are useful. Tu peux m'aider ? is friendly, Est-ce que vous pouvez m'aider ? is neutral and polite, and Pourriez-vous m'aider ? uses the conditional and is the most formal. Notice that the pronoun me shortens to m' before a vowel and sits before the infinitive.

examples.french: Tu peux m'aider deux minutes ?
examples.english: Can you help me for two minutes?

examples.french: Est-ce que vous pouvez regarder mon téléphone ?
examples.english: Can you look at my phone?

examples.french: Pourriez-vous m'expliquer le problème ?
examples.english: Could you explain the problem to me?

examples.french: Je voudrais parler à un technicien.
examples.english: I'd like to speak to a technician.

examples.french: Auriez-vous cinq minutes ?
examples.english: Would you have five minutes?

blocks.tip: Starting with Excusez-moi de vous déranger, mais… makes any request sound noticeably more polite in French.

passages.title: Au magasin de réparation
passages.french:
— Bonjour, j'ai un problème avec mon ordinateur portable.
— Bonjour. Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas exactement ?
— Il est très lent depuis la dernière mise à jour, et il plante souvent.
— Vous avez essayé de le redémarrer ?
— Oui, trois fois. Ça ne change rien.
— D'accord. Il est encore sous garantie ?
— Non, je l'ai acheté il y a trois ans.
— Alors la réparation coûtera soixante euros environ.
— C'est possible de l'avoir avant vendredi ? C'est un peu urgent.
— Le technicien le regarde demain. Je vous appelle jeudi.
passages.english:
"Hello, I have a problem with my laptop."
"Hello. What exactly is wrong?"
"It's very slow since the last update, and it crashes often."
"Have you tried restarting it?"
"Yes, three times. It doesn't change anything."
"All right. Is it still under warranty?"
"No, I bought it three years ago."
"Then the repair will cost around sixty euros."
"Is it possible to have it before Friday? It's a bit urgent."
"The technician will look at it tomorrow. I'll call you on Thursday."
